We use tools from applied microeconomics and causal inference to study how South
African households make financial decisions, and which policies would make
consumer financial markets work more efficiently and more equitably.

## Research programmes

Our work is organised into programmes. Each output below is tagged with the
programme it belongs to; use the tags to filter the list.

**Mortgage pricing in South Africa.** Access to affordable housing finance is
essential for economic mobility, yet mortgage pricing varies significantly across
applicants. This programme investigates disparities in mortgage offer
probabilities and interest rates by age, gender, marital status and first-time
buyer status, with a view to policies that promote fair and transparent lending.

**The market for funeral insurance.** Funeral insurance is one of the most widely
purchased financial products in South Africa, while life insurance remains far
less common. This programme examines the extent to which the two are substitutes,
on both the supply side — regulatory barriers and industry practice — and the
demand side, where mortality, income and intergenerational living arrangements
shape what households buy.
